title: legal redlines scratchpad - oliver garcia
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for common redlines & negotiation talking points when reviewing customer/partner agreements. Not legal advice, just notes to surface to counsel and AE.

Top priority clauses to watch (at a glance):
- Indemnification: watch for broad customer indemnities (esp. third-party claims re: data or model outputs). Counter: mutual limited indemnities; carve out negligence/gross negligence. Suggest cap: 1x/3x fees depending on risk.
- Liability cap: try to keep at least the greater of (12 months fees) or $1M for SMB; for enterprise ask for higher or carveouts for IP infringement/bodily injury. Always push to exclude breach of confidentiality/intentional misconduct from cap.
- IP ownership & license scope: ensure customer data remains theirs; Redwood retains model/IP. Watch for language that assigns model improvements or derivative models to customer. Recommended language: customer grants narrow license to use data for providing service, logging/telemetry only for ops/improvement with opt-out on training.
- Data use / training: customers increasingly ask to opt their data out of training. We need standardized opt-out language and a roadmap for handling training requests. If customer demands no training, offer contractual assurance plus fee uplift.
- Security & compliance obligations: be careful with absolute SLAs (e.g., SOC2). Accept obligation to maintain certifications in good faith. For breach notification, keep 72 hours target but no admission of liability.
- SLA & credits: avoid automatic termination based on minor SLO misses. Prefer service credits limited to a percentage of monthly fees. Can offer stronger uptime commitments for Dedicated/Private with higher pricing.
- Termination for convenience & transition assistance: watch for long transition assistance obligations and high employee-level dependencies. Limit to 30-90 days and cap fees.
- Confidentiality: standard mutual NDA ok. Watch for perpetual confidentiality on aggregated performance metrics.
- Subprocessors / third parties: require notice & right to object for security-sensitive subprocessors; offer standard list and 30-day notice for additions.
- Audit rights: limit to annual, scoped, on-site only for material risk, and require confidentiality protections. Prefer self-attestation + SOC2 report rather than full audits.
- Export controls / compliance: add standard compliance clause; customer must ensure lawful use.
- Publicity: customer logo/press releases should require mutual sign-off.

Negotiation playbook / suggested fallback positions:
- DATA TRAINING REQUESTS:
  * Customer: "Vendor may not use our data for training."
  * Our initial ask: explain technical/legal practicality and operational impact. Offer two options: 1) Standard: allow use for ops & improvement but not for model redistribution, anonymize/aggregate; 2) Opt-out: customer pays 15-30% premium, vendor will NOT use data to train production models and will segregate logs for N months.
  * Talking point: training opt-out has measurable cost; need to quantify (example: 20-40% uplift in infra + lost optimization cadence).

- INDEMNITY / LIABILITY:
  * Customer pushes for broad indemnity including outputs. Push back: cannot indemnify for outputs that vendor doesn't control (free-text outputs). Offer IP infringement indemnity for software deliverables and standard exclusion for model outputs; cap indemnity to fees.

- SLA / CREDITS / TERMINATION:
  * If customer insists on strong uptime SLA for hosted API, propose tiered SLA tied to plan: standard (99.5%) with credits; premium (99.9%) for Dedicated with stronger monitoring & runbook. For termination, limit right to persistent and uncured breaches and exclude economic reasons.

- IP ASSIGNMENT RED FLAGS:
  * If contract tries to claim derivative models or model weights trained on customer data, escalate to counsel. Our position: no assignment; license back only for customer-specific deliverables (e.g., fine-tuned, dedicated models) with clear scope.

Operational notes / redline snippets to carry into markup:
- "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train or improve Vendor models except as set forth in Section X." -> Replace with: "Vendor may use Customer Data for operations, security, and service improvement in aggregated/anonymized form; use for model training requires explicit opt-in or separate commercial terms."
- "Customer shall indemnify Vendor for any claim arising out of Customer Data." -> Flag and seek limitation to third-party IP claims and only to extent caused by Customer breach.
- Limitation of Liability: prefer: "Except for liability for (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality, (iii) IP infringement, Vendor's liability shall be limited to the greater of (A) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (B) $1,000,000."

Questions to loop in Legal (high priority):
- If customer insists on full training opt-out, what is the minimal acceptable indemnity/price uplift? Need proposed clause and pricing playbook.
- For enterprise with export control concerns (govt data), can we provide on-prem package wording that limits remote telemetry? Checklist for private deployment instead of hosted.
- For audit requests from very large customers ("audit us anytime"), what's our fallback? Need canned response: SOC2 + self-attestation + MiTM limited audit.

Practical negotiation tactics for AEs/AMs (quick bullets):
- Always ask what the customer's actual risk is and why they need the clause. Tailor solution (e.g., SOC2 evidence, opt-out, dedicated environment) rather than just pushing back.
- Use pricing as a lever: stronger contractual commitments (no-training, higher SLA, bespoke security) => price uplift and longer lead time.
- Offer alternatives before flat no: e.g., "we can scope a private instance" or "we can provide data deletion on request and dedicated retention windows."
- For legal-heavy customers, suggest a 3-way call with Legal + Engineering to talk through technical mitigations (how we isolate training data, deletion procedures).

Quick links / refs for counsel: (put these in the review PR)
- Confluence: Platform Security Requirements (link above)
- Past signed addendum with BigCo (JIRA-OPS-1234) — see termination & training opt-out language we conceded.
- PR #56 in terms repo: earlier draft of "data training" clause we negotiated.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft reusable opt-out language for training (two variants: strict opt-out + paid opt-out) and circulate to Legal + Product.
- Compile list of standard subprocessors and propose 30-day notice clause.
- Create pricing rubric for opt-out / enhanced SLA (eng + finance input).
- Follow up with Jordan on the BigCo addendum playbook.

Unresolved points / risk areas to watch later:
- Do we need to add explicit non-attribution clause for model improvements when aggregated telemetry is used?
- How to quantify training cost uplift more precisely for commercial conversations? (ask Applied ML for a rough %).

End scratchpad.
